key_insight: CiteGuard-RAG adds runtime validation to retrieval-augmented generation so answers are not just informed by evidence, but also citation-valid and grounded enough to trust. If the system cannot validate support, it can refuse or regenerate the answer once.
problem_solved: Standard RAG systems can retrieve relevant documents but still produce unsupported claims, incorrect citations, or overconfident answers when evidence is weak. This paper addresses the gap between "having retrieved evidence" and "actually producing grounded, verifiable answers."
method: Uses hybrid semantic-lexical retrieval to improve evidence coverage and relevance.
Constrains generation so answers must align with available citations.
Performs sentence-level grounding validation at runtime to check whether each claim is supported.
Applies a single-pass regeneration or refusal strategy when validation fails.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical framework for building more reliable RAG systems in high-stakes or knowledge-sensitive settings. It helps reduce hallucinations, improve citation quality, and make model refusals more principled and auditable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing retrieval -> constrained generation -> grounding validation -> regeneration/refusal
Icon set for document retrieval, citation links, validation checkmarks, and warning/refusal
Before/after comparison of standard RAG vs CiteGuard-RAG answer quality
Sentence-level evidence alignment chart highlighting supported vs unsupported claims
paper_title: CiteGuard-RAG: A Validation-Centered AI System for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering
paper_authors: Sumit Barua, Guan Hong, Halil Dursunoglu, Charles Rodgers, Alvis Fong
